propositions: A new discovery submodule must define immutable typed plan and result structures with six distinct unit outcomes (success, resumed, skipped, shed, failed, cancelled) to distinguish clean execution from failed, cancelled, skipped, budget-shed, or resumed criterion work.

The discovery executor must implement dependency-aware scheduling with deterministic ascending-rank shedding, usage accumulation, and checkpoint eligibility (success and content-identical resumed only), ensuring later-raised failures do not erase earlier successes.

A versioned digest-complete envelope covering material, code, effective-policy, prompt, contract, model, mode, topology, dependencies, and namespace version must enable stable deterministic identity and prevent legacy/mismatched envelopes from round-tripping as reusable.

Given systemic config/provider-init failure or cancellation, the executor must stop scheduling, return exact completed-failed-cancelled accounting, and mark already-dispatched calls by their true outcome with real usage while not-yet-dispatched units become cancelled.

Positive explicit budget must shed work in deterministic order (dependency rank, then stable unit id) producing identical shed sets across runs; omission is uncapped and zero is rejected rather than disabled.
The stored trace must serialize normalized outcome metadata and lineage without raw prompts, ticket/context bodies, provider responses, or secrets, and review result schemas remain unchanged.
